cards.explanation: The answer is an angel of the Lord came down from heaven. Matthew says, “Suddenly there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven…” The shaking and the angel arrive together. Then the angel rolls the stone away and sits on it.

The answer is True. The angel descends from heaven, rolls away the stone, and sits on it. He doesn't just move it, he takes a seat on it. Matthew tells us the stone is gone from the entrance, and the angel is perched on top.

The answer is that they tremble and become like dead men. Matthew says the guards trembled in fear of him and became like dead men. These were the ones posted to watch the tomb, and they go still as stones. That tells you, friends, how big this moment was.

The answer is that He has risen just as He said. The angel says, “He is not here; He has risen, just as He said!” Jesus had told His disciples that He would be killed and on the third day be raised to life (Matthew 16:21). So the angel is pointing back to what Jesus already said.
The answer is False. The angel says, “Come, see the place where He lay.” So the women are invited to come and look, not to keep their distance. Then he sends them off to tell the disciples.

The answer is Galilee. The angel tells the women to say that Jesus has risen from the dead and is going ahead of the disciples into Galilee. Then he adds, “There you will see Him.” He even finishes with, “See, I have told you.”
The answer is joy. Matthew says the women hurried away from the tomb in fear and great joy. Both feelings are packed into one run. And they ran to tell His disciples.

The answer is Jesus Himself. Matthew says, “Suddenly Jesus met them and said, ‘Greetings!’” The women were still on their way to tell the disciples when it happened. They didn't have to wait to see Him.

The answer is that they grasp His feet and worship Him. Matthew says they came to Him, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him. They don't just look at Him, they take hold of His feet. I think they wanted to be sure He was really there.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee.” Notice what He calls the disciples, friends. After everything that happened, they are still His brothers.

The answer is a large sum of money. After the chief priests had met with the elders and formed a plan, they gave the soldiers a large sum of money. Then they told the soldiers what to say. I think a plan that needs that much cash has a problem.

The answer is asleep. The chief priests tell the soldiers to say, “His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were asleep.” That's the story the soldiers were handed. It's the report they were told to give.

The answer is True. The chief priests tell the soldiers, “If this report reaches the governor, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble.” So the soldiers get cash and a promise. That's the whole deal.

The answer is False. Matthew says, “So the guards took the money and did as they were instructed.” They accepted the money and then told the story the chief priests gave them. And Matthew says, “…this account has been circulated among the Jews to this very day.”
The answer is False. Matthew says, “When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted.” So there was worship, and there was also doubt among some of them. Jesus comes to them anyway.

The answer is all authority in heaven and on earth. Jesus says, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.” That's the opening of what He tells the eleven. Everything He says after it rests on that.
The answer is people of all nations. Jesus says, “Therefore go and make disciples of all nations…” That's a big field, friends, and it starts with the eleven standing on that mountain.

The answers are baptize and teach. Jesus says to make disciples, “…baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit…” That's the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit named together in one line. Then He says, “…and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you.” It's about obeying all He commanded.
The answer is always, to the end of the age. Jesus says, “And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” There's no gap in it. He doesn't say when that end comes, and neither do I.
